function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to clone repositories, inspect their contents, or make commits to your GitHub account.  
What I can do is give you step‑by‑step instructions (and even generate the files you’ll need) so you can carry out the whole workflow on your own machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> **Tip** – If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the URL with `https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`.

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & generate artefacts

### 2.1 Create/Update a Dockerfile

A typical Node.js “welcome” app probably contains an `app.js` (or `index.js`) and a `package.json`.  
Below is a minimal Dockerfile that works for most Node.js projects:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

COPY . .

EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

If you want me to generate this file automatically, let me know the directory name (e.g., `"nodejs-welcome"`). I can then call the `create_a_docker_file` function for you.

### 2.2 Generate Kubernetes YAMLs

Assuming the container listens on port 3000 and you want two replicas exposed as a LoadBalancer:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
# k8s/service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

Again, if you’d like me to generate these files automatically, just tell me the directory name (e.g., `"nodejs-welcome"`).

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

Make sure you store your Docker Hub credentials in the repository’s *Settings → Secrets* (`DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`).

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml k8s/service.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

---

### Optional: Let me generate the files for you

If you’d like me to create the Dockerfile and Kubernetes YAMLs automatically, just reply with the directory name (relative to the current working directory) and I’ll invoke the helper functions for you. For example:

```text
Directory name: nodejs-welcome
```

Once I’ve generated the files, you can copy the output into the appropriate locations in your repo.
